the identification of putative MAV target genes provides important clues for understanding MAV pathogenic potential and that the highly efficient MAV-induced tumorigensis results from the alteration and activation of multiple genes in differentiating cells.

the MAV-induced tumor is a model of Wilms' tumor and that the MAV provirus integrates in the vicinity of several genes that have a role in the control of signaling and proliferation of the kidney blastemal cells and that the tumor cells have a high level of ADAMTS1 expression.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of new genes that could be involved in the development and/or progression of Wilms' tumor and other cancers.
the identification of genes that are involved in the control cell signaling and proliferation, and that are altered during tumor development.

the identification of genes involved in the development of Wilms' tumor, a pediatric renal neoplasia, and with the characterization of the molecular mechanisms that are involved in the development and progression of this tumor.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MAV-induced tumors are a model of the pediatric nephroblastoma, and that they can be used as a tool to identify new oncogenes and suppressors of tumor growth.

MAV-induced nephroblastosma represents a model of tumor progression in which the initial tumorigenesis is followed by multiple steps of tumor progression, each one being associated with the acquisition of new genetic alterations.
the MAV-induced tumorigenicity results from the alteration by proviral insertion of multiple genes that play a role in the differentiation of the blastema and the progression of the tumor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MAV-induced tumor represents a good model to study Wilms' tumor pathogenesis and that the MAV integration sites are good candidates for the identification of new oncogenes and tumour suppressors.
we have identified several new genes involved in the development of Wilms' tumor, and that these genes may have a role in the establishment of the tumor.

the integration of MAV proviral sequences occurs preferentially in the vicinity of host genes that are important for cell proliferation and differentiation, and that the MAV-induced tumors represent the result of the alteration of multiple host genes.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we have identified a new gene, ADAMTS1, that is upregulated in MAV nephroblastomas and that we are now characterizing its role in the development of the kidney and in the establishment of nephroblastomas.

the MAV-induced tumor is a unique animal model for studying the mechanisms of tumor initiation and progression, as well as for testing the therapeutic potential of new drugs in a tumor that is histopathologically and genetically similar to human Wilms' tumors.

the MAV-induced tumorigenic process involves multiple genes and pathways that are involved in the control and maintenance of normal kidney development and function, and in the control of the proliferation, differentiation and survival of blastemal cells.
